CLM14994555102016-08-1820Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS:This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:
1. (Currently Amended) A computer-implemented method of assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the method comprising: receiving a patient-specific anatomic model of a patient's visceral vasculature, including visceral vasculature of the patient's visceral organs and bowel; determining a location of modeled visceral vasculature in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining, for the location in the patient-specific anatomic model, a blood flow characteristic defining a characteristic of blood flow through the location in the patient- specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determininq a blood flow demand of the determined tissue reqion: determininq, usinq the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic associated with the determined location of the modeled visceral vasculature and/or the determined tissue reqion; and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, or generating a risk score defining a risk of-2-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic.currently amendedIndependent
2. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.previously presentedDependent
3. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising: receiving the patient-specific anatomic model including at least a portion of the patient's bowel; further determining the blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel; and determining the assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined blood flow demand and the determined blood flow characteristic at the location in the patient-specific model of the patient's visceral vasculature.currently amendedDependent
4. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 3,further including: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions;-3-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.previously presentedDependent
5. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising: determining the blood flow characteristic at the location of the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature using a fluid simulation or blood flow characteristics associated with one or more other patients.previously presentedDependent
6. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising: receiving a physiological state associated with the patient; and generating the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's [[bowl]] bowel or generating the risk score for risk of disease for the patient's viscera or bowel, further based on the received physiological state.currently amendedDependent
7. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 6,further comprising: modifying a geometry of the patient-specific anatomic model or modifying the received physiological state of the patient;-4-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient- specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient; and generating an updated assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel or generating a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient.previously presentedDependent
8. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising: determining the risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, wherein the risk of disease may include includes risk of one or more of mesenteric ischemia, intestinal ischemia, ischemic colitis, abdominal pain, gangrene, bowel perforation, sepsis, stricture, mesenteric ischemia, inflammatory conditions.currently amendedDependent
9. (Currently Amended) A system for assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the system comprising: a data storage device storing instructions for assessment of ischemic colitis; and a processor configured to execute the instructions to perform a method including:-5-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000receiving a patient-specific anatomic model of a patient's visceral vasculature, including visceral vasculature of the patient's visceral organs and bowel; determining a location of modeled visceral vasculature in the patient- specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining, for the location in the patient-specific anatomic model, a blood flow characteristic defining a characteristic of blood flow through the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; and determininq a blood flow demand of the determined tissue region; determininq, usinq the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic associated with the determined location of the modeled visceral vasculature and/or the determined tissue reqion; and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel_ based on the determined blood flow characteristic, or generating a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic.-6-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000currently amendedIndependent
10. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.previously presentedDependent
11. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for: receiving the patient-specific anatomic model including at least a portion of the patient's bowel; further determining the blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel; and determining the assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined blood flow demand and the determined blood flow characteristic at the location in the patient-specific model of the patient's visceral vasculature.currently amendedDependent
12. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 11, wherein the system is further configured for: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions; determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.-7-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000previously presentedDependent
13. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for: determining the blood flow characteristic at the location of the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature using a fluid simulation or blood flow characteristics associated with one or more other patients.previously presentedDependent
14. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for: receiving a physiological state associated with the patient; and generating the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's bowl or generating the risk score for risk of disease for the patient's viscera or bowel, further based on the received physiological state.previously presentedDependent
15. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 14, wherein the system is further configured for: modifying a geometry of the patient-specific anatomic model or modifying the received physiological state of the patient; determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient- specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient; and generating an updated assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel or generating a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of-8-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient.previously presentedDependent
16. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for: determining the risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, wherein the risk of disease may include risk of one or more of ischemic colitis, abdominal pain, gangrene, bowel perforation, sepsis, stricture, mesenteric ischemia, inflammatory conditions.previously presentedDependent
17. (Currently Amended) A non-transitory computer readable medium for use on a computer system containing computer-executable programming instructions for performing a method of assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the method comprising: receiving a patient-specific anatomic model of a patient's visceral vasculature, including visceral vasculature of the patient's visceral organs and bowel; determining a location of modeled visceral vasculature in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature;-9-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000determining, for the location in the patient-specific anatomic model, a blood flow characteristic defining a characteristic of blood flow through the location in the patient- specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determininq a blood flow demand of the determined tissue region; determining, using the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic associated with the determined location of the modeled visceral vasculature and/or the determined tissue region; and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, or generating a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic.currently amendedIndependent
18. (Previously Presented) The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 17, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.previously presentedDependent
19. (Currently Amended) The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 17, the method further comprising:-10-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000receiving the patient-specific anatomic model including at least a portion of the patient's bowel; further determining the blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel; and determining the assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined blood flow demand and the determined blood flow characteristic at the location in the patient-specific model of the patient's visceral vasculature.currently amendedDependent
20. (Previously Presented) The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 19, the method further comprising: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions; determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.-11-previously presentedDependent
